number.why: The numerical HR 0.89 (95% CI 0.70–1.13) is correct for edoxaban versus warfarin, but SERVED_CONFIRMED is not justified for the served intention-to-treat population. The registry explicitly assigns this primary outcome to mITT. The ruling recognizes this discrepancy but treats it as an imprecise label; the packet does not establish equivalence to ITT. The supported estimate is the reported HR for mITT over 12 months.

quotes.span: The primary efficacy outcome was recurrent symptomatic venous thromboembolism.

Edoxaban was noninferior to warfarin with respect to the primary efficacy outcome, which occurred in 130 patients in the edoxaban group (3.2%) and 146 patients in the warfarin group (3.5%) (hazard ratio, 0.89; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.70 to 1.13; P<0.001 for noninferiority).
TIME FRAME: 12 months from time of randomization | POPULATION: (mITT) modified Intent To Treat Analysis Set

entry.why: Eligibility explicitly establishes adults with imaging-confirmed acute symptomatic proximal DVT and/or symptomatic PE, matching the question's entry population. The mITT discrepancy concerns the analysis population, not entry eligibility.

missed: The consequential issue is the unresolved ITT versus mITT mismatch already identified but not enforced by the ruling. The quoted registry analysis also establishes a stratification-adjusted Cox time-to-first-event HR and supplies more precise confidence limits, consistent with the rounded abstract values; it does not establish an ITT estimate.
